sections.title: Microporous Substrate Holding
sections.description: Sample flatness sounds like a small detail until it distorts an entire coating run, and most sheet coaters solve it with extra manual steps to fixate the substrate in place. FOM vectorSC's proprietary substrate holder takes a different approach, using a microporous structure that provides homogeneous suction across the substrate itself. That suction holds the sample flat directly, without needing the extra fixation steps typically required elsewhere, saving time on every single run rather than just occasionally. The result is excellent substrate flatness as a built-in property of the system, not something the operator has to work to achieve each time.

sections.title: Integrated Pump and Remote Operation
sections.description: Precursor delivery and remote access are usually two separate problems. FOM vectorSC solves them together by building the pump directly into the tool and pairing it with cloud-based control.
body: Because the pump is integrated rather than external, precursor delivery becomes part of the same controlled system as substrate positioning and coating parameters, rather than a separate piece of hardware to manage alongside it. Cloud-based software then extends that control beyond the physical lab, enabling genuine remote operation and diagnostics, useful for teams checking in on a run from elsewhere, or for troubleshooting support without needing someone physically present at the machine.

A protocol library saves your deposition process in full, so recalling it reproduces the same run with high precision and gives you real insight into which variables actually moved between attempts. A microporous substrate holder provides homogeneous suction across flexible or rigid substrates, removing the manual fixation steps that usually eat into setup time between samples. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, run through software-integrated pump control, for a systematic, accelerated workflow rather than manual positioning guesswork. Add post-deposition units, drying, annealing, compressed gas for quick-drying, and docking modules, and the standalone tool grows into a small-scale pilot processing line, built to carry your research from lab-scale proof of concept toward a higher technology readiness level.

A microporous substrate holder applies homogeneous suction across the substrate surface, holding flexible or rigid materials in place without the taping, clipping, or manual fixturing that typically adds setup time before a run can even start. The slot-die head itself moves on automated vertical and lateral axes, coordinated with software-integrated pump control, turning what would otherwise be manual positioning into a repeatable, systematic process.

sections.title: Automated Substrate Handling and Slot-Die Positioning
sections.description: Two things determine whether a coating run stays consistent from sample to sample: how the substrate is held, and how precisely the head is positioned over it. FOM alphaSC handles both automatically. The microporous substrate holder applies suction evenly across the surface, which is what lets it hold both flexible and rigid substrates without the manual fixturing steps that would otherwise vary slightly between operators or runs. From there, the slot-die head's automated vertical and lateral movement, coordinated with software-integrated pump control, positions and runs the coating pass the same way every time, rather than depending on manual alignment.
